  - text: CLASS 12 • THREE-DIMENSIONAL GEOMETRY
  - heading "Point-Normal Form" [level=1]
  - paragraph: "A plane through point P₀ with normal vector n:"
  - strong: n · (r - r₀) = 0
  - text: 18 min ADVANCED CONCEPT geometry2d
  - main:
    - complementary:
      - heading "INTERACTIVE POINT-NORMAL BUILDER" [level=3]
      - article:
        - heading "1. Point on plane P₀" [level=2]
        - paragraph: P₀(x₀,y₀,z₀)
        - group:
          - text: x
          - spinbutton "p x": "1"
          - text: "y"
          - spinbutton "p y": "-2"
          - text: z
          - spinbutton "p z": "3"
      - article:
        - heading "2. Normal vector n" [level=2]
        - paragraph: n=(a,b,c)
        - group:
          - text: x
          - spinbutton "n x": "2"
          - text: "y"
          - spinbutton "n y": "1"
          - text: z
          - spinbutton "n z": "-1"
        - strong: n ≠ 0 ✓ |n|=2.4495
      - article:
        - heading "3. Test point r (draggable)" [level=2]
        - paragraph: R(x,y,z)
        - group:
          - text: x
          - spinbutton "r x": "0.4"
          - text: "y"
          - spinbutton "r y": "-0.6"
          - text: z
          - spinbutton "r z": "1.8"
      - text: Quick picks
      - button "On plane"
      - button "Off plane (+)"
      - button "Off plane (-)"
      - button "Random"
      - button "Reset all":
        - img
        - text: Reset all
    - article:
      - heading "3D VISUALIZATION" [level=3]
      - button "Rotate"
      - button "Reset":
        - img
        - text: Reset
      - img "Point-normal form plane visualization": P₀(1, -2, 3) R(0.4, -0.6, 1.8) n=(2, 1, -1)
      - checkbox "Show plane" [checked]
      - text: Show plane
      - checkbox "Show normal" [checked]
      - text: Show normal
      - checkbox "Show displacement" [checked]
      - text: Show displacement
      - checkbox "Show perpendicular" [checked]
      - text: Show perpendicular
      - checkbox "Show axes" [checked]
      - text: Show axes
      - paragraph: Drag R to see how r-r₀ stays in the plane exactly when it is perpendicular to n.
    - article:
      - heading "POINT-NORMAL EQUATION" [level=3]
      - strong: n · (r-r₀) = 0
      - paragraph: "Substitute: (2, 1, -1) · ((x,y,z)-(1, -2, 3))=0"
      - paragraph: "Expand and simplify:"
      - strong: 2x + y - z + 3 = 0
    - article:
      - heading "TEST POINT CHECKER" [level=3]
      - text: n · (r-r₀) 1.4 Signed residual ax+by+cz+d 1.4 Perpendicular distance 0.5715
      - paragraph: "Vector r-r₀=(-0.6, 1.4, -1.2); status: Off plane"
    - article:
      - heading "FROM POINT-NORMAL TO ax+by+cz+d=0" [level=3]
      - paragraph: n · (r-r₀)=0 ⇒ ax+by+cz-(ax₀+by₀+cz₀)=0
      - strong: d=-(ax₀+by₀+cz₀)=3
      - strong: "General form: 2x + y - z + 3 = 0"
    - article:
      - heading "NORMAL REVERSAL (EQUIVALENCE)" [level=3]
      - paragraph: (-n) · (r-r₀)=0 is identical to n · (r-r₀)=0.
      - button "Reverse normal"
      - strong: "-2x - y + z - 3=0"
    - article:
      - heading "COMMON MISCONCEPTION" [level=3]
      - paragraph: "Wrong: n · r=0. This describes a plane through the origin only."
      - text: Always use n · (r-r₀)=0 for a general point P₀.
    - article:
      - heading "ALL IN-PLANE DISPLACEMENTS ARE PERPENDICULAR TO n" [level=3]
      - paragraph: For any in-plane point R, r-r₀ is perpendicular to n.
      - paragraph: "Proof: n · (r-r₀)=0 exactly states orthogonality."
    - article:
      - heading "WORKED EXAMPLE" [level=3]
      - list:
        - listitem: "Point-normal: (2, 1, -1) · ((x,y,z)-(1, -2, 3))=0"
        - listitem: Expand component products.
        - listitem: "Simplify: 2x + y - z + 3 = 0"
    - article:
      - heading "PRACTICE YOURSELF" [level=3]
      - text: 1. Value of n · (r-r₀) for a point on plane?
      - textbox "Practice answer 1"
      - button "Check"
      - text: 2. Is R=(2,-1,2) on this plane?
      - textbox "Practice answer 2"
      - button "Check"
      - text: 3. Signed residual for R=(2,-1,2)?
      - textbox "Practice answer 3"
      - button "Check"
      - text: 4. Distance from R=(2,-1,2)?
      - textbox "Practice answer 4"
      - button "Check"
    - heading "MORE CONCEPTS (VERIFIED)" [level=3]
    - article:
      - text: Direction lying in plane
      - paragraph: Any d with n · d=0 lies in the plane.
    - article:
      - text: Cross product normal
      - paragraph: If u,v lie in the plane, u x v is parallel to n.
    - article:
      - text: Scalar triple product
      - paragraph: For an in-plane displacement d, n · d=0.
    - article:
      - text: Distance formula
      - paragraph: Distance = |ax+by+cz+d|/|n|.
